meta.purpose: Topic-keyed equations, symbol definitions and conceptual setup steps for the right-hand panel.
meta.notation: The professor's own notation throughout: a is fixed, b is variable; fixed cost and profit are never unitized.
meta.sources: study-guide.md, which was built from his class sessions, practice problems and handouts.

home.eq: Revenue - Variable Cost - Fixed Cost = Profit
home.note: His "One" Formula, also called the Home Equation. Every CVP question is this one equation with a different unknown.

equations.eq: Sale Price(Volume) - VC Rate(Volume) - Total FC = Profit
symbols: Sale Price: price per unit
VC Rate: variable cost per unit
Total FC: fixed cost in total, never per unit
Volume: units

equations.eq: CM/unit(Volume) - Total FC = Profit
symbols: CM/unit: Sale Price - VC Rate

equations.eq: Revenue - VC%(Revenue) - Total FC = Profit
symbols: VC%: variable cost as a share of revenue

equations.eq: Break-even Volume = Total FC / CM per unit
symbols: Profit set to zero

equations.eq: Break-even Revenue = Total FC / CM ratio
symbols: CM ratio = 1 - VC ratio

equations.eq: Target Volume = (Total FC + Target Profit) / CM per unit
symbols: Target Profit sits beside fixed cost in the numerator, nothing else changes

setup: Read what the question wants: units, revenue, or profit. That picks which form you use.
List the four inputs: Sale Price, VC Rate, Total FC, Volume. One of them is the unknown.
Given per-unit figures, work in CM per unit. Given percentages, work in CM ratio.
Set Profit to zero for break even, or to the target for a target question.
Solve, then round volumes UP to the next whole unit. You cannot sell part of a unit.
Trap: never unitize fixed cost or profit. Fixed cost stays a total.

home.eq: Revenue - Variable Cost - Fixed Cost = Profit
home.note: His "One" Formula, also called the Home Equation. Every CVP question is this one equation with a different unknown.

equations.eq: Margin of Safety = Current Volume - Break-even Volume
symbols: In units or in dollars, same subtraction

equations.eq: MoS dollars = MoS units x Sale Price
symbols: Keep the UNROUNDED break even here

equations.eq: How far above break even = MoS / Break-even Volume
symbols: Denominator is break even

equations.eq: How far can sales fall = MoS / Current Volume
symbols: Denominator is current sales

setup: Compute break even first. The margin of safety is a second step, never a first one.
Decide which percentage the words ask for. He asks for both versions on different questions.
"How far can sales fall before we lose money" divides by CURRENT sales.
"How far are we above break even" divides by BREAK EVEN.
Trap: for the dollar answer, use the unrounded break-even volume. Rounding first loses dollars.

home.eq: Revenue - Variable Cost - Fixed Cost = Profit
home.note: His "One" Formula, also called the Home Equation. Every CVP question is this one equation with a different unknown.

equations.eq: Operating Income (pretax) = After-tax Net Income / (1 - tax rate)
symbols: Divide, never multiply. You must earn MORE pretax than you keep.

equations.eq: Target Volume = (Total FC + Pretax Target) / CM per unit
symbols: Gross up to pretax BEFORE the target enters the equation

setup: Spot whether the target is stated after tax. If it is, gross it up first.
Pretax = After-tax / (1 - t). Do this before touching the CVP equation.
Put the pretax figure beside Total FC in the numerator.
Solve for volume and round up.
Trap: multiplying by (1 - t) instead of dividing is the wrong answer sitting in the options.

home.eq: Revenue - Variable Cost - Fixed Cost = Profit
home.note: His "One" Formula, also called the Home Equation. Every CVP question is this one equation with a different unknown.

equations.eq: Operating Income (pretax) = After-tax Net Income / (1 - tax rate)
symbols: Same gross-up

equations.eq: Target Net Income = Equity x Required ROE
symbols: ROE uses EQUITY

equations.eq: Target Net Income = Total Assets x Required ROA
symbols: ROA uses TOTAL ASSETS

setup: Read whether the return is on equity or on assets. That picks the base you multiply.
Multiply the base by the required rate to get the after-tax income the owner wants.
Gross that up to pretax by dividing by (1 - t).
Then it is an ordinary target-profit CVP question.
Trap: using total assets when the question said equity, or the reverse.

home.eq: Revenue - Variable Cost - Fixed Cost = Profit
home.note: His "One" Formula, also called the Home Equation. Every CVP question is this one equation with a different unknown.

equations.eq: Basket method: Basket CM = sum over products of (mix units x CM per unit)
symbols: Mix is the UNIT ratio, for example 12 to 1

equations.eq: Break-even Baskets = Total FC / Basket CM
symbols: Leave this UNROUNDED

equations.eq: Product units = Baskets x that product's mix number
symbols: Unpack FIRST, then round each product up

equations.eq: Weighted average method: Weighted CM = sum of (unit-volume weight x CM per unit)
symbols: Weights are shares of total UNITS

equations.eq: Revenue method: Break-even Revenue = (Total FC + Target Profit) / (1 - VC ratio)
symbols: VC ratio = Total Variable Cost / Total Revenue

equations.eq: Product revenue = Break-even Revenue x that product's REVENUE share
symbols: Revenue share, never the unit mix

setup: Identify the mix and whether it is given in units or in revenue. They are different numbers.
Pick a method. All three agree if you do them right; the basket method is his default.
Build the basket from the unit mix, then divide Total FC by basket contribution margin.
Do NOT round the baskets. Baskets are a counting device, not a quantity.
Unpack to each product, then round each product up.
Trap: splitting a REVENUE answer by the unit mix. Revenue splits by revenue share.
There is no single multi-product break even. Change the mix and the answer changes.

home.note: The same equation rearranged into total cost. a is fixed, b is variable, his letters.

equations.eq: Total Cost = Variable Cost + Fixed Cost
symbols: Only two behaviours exist in this course

equations.eq: Variable Cost = VC Rate x Volume
symbols: VC Rate is constant per unit, total rises with volume

equations.eq: Total FC is constant in total
symbols: Fixed cost PER UNIT falls as volume rises, which is why he never unitizes it

equations.eq: Rebuilding from a GAAP statement: Total FC = Total Cost - (VC per unit x Volume)
symbols: Cost of goods sold is not variable cost and selling and admin is not fixed cost. Both lines are mixtures.

setup: Decide what each cost does when VOLUME moves, not where it sits on the income statement.
Add up every variable cost per unit to get one VC Rate.
Multiply VC Rate by volume for total variable cost.
Total cost minus total variable cost leaves Total FC.
Trap: a GAAP statement cannot be used for CVP as it stands. Rebuild the split first.
Trap: step costs are fixed within a range and jump between ranges. Work inside the right range.

home.note: The same equation rearranged into total cost. a is fixed, b is variable, his letters.

equations.eq: b = variable rate = (High cost - Low cost) / (High activity - Low activity)
symbols: b is variable

equations.eq: a = total fixed = High cost - b(High activity)
symbols: a is fixed

equations.eq: Check: a = Low cost - b(Low activity)
symbols: Both points must give the same a

setup: Pick the high and low points by ACTIVITY, never by cost. This is the trap he plants most often.
Subtract to get b, the variable rate per unit of activity.
Put b back into the HIGH point to get a.
Check a at the LOW point. If the two disagree, you picked the points by cost.
Only two points are used. Every other row is ignored by design.

home.note: Intercept a is fixed cost, slope b is the variable rate. The same a and b as high-low.

equations.eq: Point estimate = Intercept + Slope x Activity
symbols: Use the PRINTED, rounded coefficients

equations.eq: Interval = Point Estimate +/- ( t x the appropriate standard error )
symbols: Three standard errors exist on the output. Pick the right one.

equations.eq: Interval on a COEFFICIENT uses that coefficient's own standard error
symbols: The SE on its row

equations.eq: Interval on TOTAL COST uses the regression's standard error
symbols: The Standard Error in the summary block

equations.eq: t = coefficient / its own standard error
symbols: t at or above 2 is useful, above 3 near certain

equations.eq: Degrees of freedom = n - 2
symbols: 8 observations gives df = 6

setup: Read what the interval is around: a coefficient, or a predicted total cost.
That choice picks the standard error. Using the wrong one is the whole question.
Get t from his table at n - 2 degrees of freedom: 70% 1.134, 80% 1.440, 90% 1.943, 95% 2.447.
Multiply t by the standard error for the half-width, then add and subtract.
For a total-cost interval, build the point estimate first from the printed coefficients.
Trap: R squared says how much variation is explained, not whether the driver causes the cost.
He says "confidence interval around this estimate". He never says "prediction interval".

home.eq: DOL = Total Contribution Margin / Operating Profit
home.note: Dollars over dollars. Never the CM ratio, never a percentage, never revenue.

equations.eq: DOL x % change in Revenue = % change in Operating Profit
symbols: The reason DOL is worth knowing

equations.eq: Total CM = Revenue - Total Variable Cost
symbols: Numerator

equations.eq: Operating Profit = Total CM - Total FC
symbols: Denominator

setup: Build the full income statement in totals: revenue, total variable cost, total CM, fixed cost, profit.
Divide total contribution margin by operating profit.
To answer a sensitivity question, multiply DOL by the percentage change in revenue.
Trap: DOL is computed at ONE volume. It changes the moment volume changes.
Nearer break even, DOL grows without limit. Far above it, DOL approaches 1.

home.eq: DOL = Total Contribution Margin / Operating Profit
home.note: Dollars over dollars. Never the CM ratio, never a percentage, never revenue.

equations.eq: High leverage = large Total FC, low VC Rate
symbols: Bigger contribution margin, bigger swing

equations.eq: Low leverage = small Total FC, high VC Rate
symbols: Safer, but capped upside

equations.eq: Indifference volume = Fixed option cost / (VC Rate saved per unit)
symbols: Where a fixed-cost option and a variable-cost option cost the same

setup: Name which structure each option is: more fixed, or more variable.
Say what that does to contribution margin per unit and to Total FC.
State the consequence in both directions: more upside per unit, more downside below break even.
If the question asks which is better, the honest answer names the volume it depends on.
Trap: DOL is a point-in-time reading; operating leverage is the cost structure behind it.

home.eq: Cost per unit of production = Total cost of that input / Units of production for that input
home.note: His term is "units of production". "Equivalent units" appears nowhere in his materials.

equations.eq: Materials units of production = units sold + ALL units in process
symbols: Materials go in at the start, so work in process counts in full

equations.eq: Conversion units of production = units sold + (units in process x percent complete)
symbols: Labor and overhead accrue as work proceeds

equations.eq: Cost expensed = cost per unit x units sold
symbols: Goes to the income statement

equations.eq: Cost in inventory = cost per unit x units of production still in process
symbols: Stays on the balance sheet

equations.eq: Tie-out: expensed + inventory = total spent
symbols: If it does not tie, a denominator is wrong

setup: Separate the inputs: materials on one denominator, labor and overhead on another.
Count materials units of production: finished plus every unit started.
Count conversion units of production: finished plus partial units at their percent complete.
Divide each total cost by its own denominator.
Split each into expensed and inventory, then check that the two add back to what was spent.
Trap: one denominator for everything. Materials and conversion almost never share one.

home.eq: Allocated cost = Allocation rate x Driver quantity
home.note: Allocation moves cost between objects. It creates nothing and destroys nothing.

equations.eq: Allocation rate = Total cost in the pool / Total driver quantity
symbols: One rate per pool

equations.eq: Cost object: the thing you are asking "what does this cost me?" about
symbols: A product, a client, a line

equations.eq: Driver: the activity that actually causes the cost to move
symbols: Choose it because it drives, not because it is handy

setup: Name the cost object and the pool before touching any arithmetic.
Pick the driver that causes the cost, then compute one rate for the pool.
Multiply the rate by each object's driver quantity.
Check that the allocations add back to the pool.
Trap: an allocated figure is not a relevant cost for a short-term decision. Use incremental for that.

home.eq: Incremental Profit = Revenue added - Variable Cost added - Fixed Cost added
home.note: The question is always "what changes if we do this?". Only what changes is relevant.

equations.eq: Outsourced structure: no fixed cost, so break even is ZERO units
symbols: No downside, and no leverage either

equations.eq: Forge structure: fixed cost enters, so break even and leverage both appear
symbols: More upside per unit, real losses below break even

equations.eq: Break even = Total FC / CM per unit
symbols: Same home equation, applied to each future

setup: State which cost structure each option is before computing anything.
Compute break even and margin of safety under each.
Say what the structure does in BOTH directions: upside and downside.
End on the judgement the numbers cannot make: how confident is she in the volume?
Word limits are tight. One clause per idea, no preamble, no restating the question.

home.eq: Incremental Profit = Revenue added - Variable Cost added - Fixed Cost added
home.note: The question is always "what changes if we do this?". Only what changes is relevant.

equations.eq: Incremental operating income = added revenue - added variable cost - added fixed cost
symbols: Discretionary items, such as her own salary, stay OUT of the decision

equations.eq: Payback = Investment / periodic cash or income flow
symbols: A length of time, not a value

equations.eq: Allocated view: gross margin after spreading shared cost on a driver
symbols: Changes appearance, changes no cash and no total profit

equations.eq: Multi-product break even: basket method on the 12 to 1 unit mix
symbols: Then unpack and round each product up

setup: Answer the incremental question on incremental numbers only.
Exclude discretionary costs she does not have to incur; depreciation is not discretionary.
Then look at the allocated view separately, because appearance matters to outsiders.
Say what the allocation does NOT change: total profit and cash.
Trap: "the allocation is arbitrary so ignore it" is the wrong answer. He never says ignore it.

home.note: Individual. Proctorio. One handwritten 8.5 x 11 sheet. Excel allowed but the workbook must start blank.

equations.eq: Not permitted: GoalSeek, Solver, any AI resource
symbols: Named in the logistics sheet

equations.eq: Rounding: break-even and target volumes round UP
symbols: You never lose points for a rounding error

equations.eq: The two case items are capped at 50 and 90 words
symbols: The cap is the hardest part of those items

setup: Open with the integrity statement, item 1, worth zero points.
Work the computational items in blueprint order; they are the 80 points.
Leave time for items 17 and 18. The word limits need drafting, not dumping.
Keep Excel blank at the start and build each calculation fresh.
